msgMainDropLabel: Drop audio files to add them
msgMainListEmpty: No files yet. Drag audio files onto this window.
msgStgAboutDesc: is a yaiol Rust app template.
msgMainNoFfmpeg: The conversion engine (ffmpeg) was not found. Put it next to the app, or install it and add it to the PATH.
msgDstPatternHint: Click a tag to add it. A slash makes a sub-folder.
msgDstSourceFixed: This entry always writes next to the original file and keeps its name.
msgPrsRingtoneLimit: An iPhone ringtone is cut to 40 seconds, the longest iOS accepts.
lblDstKeepStructure: Keep the folder structure when converting a folder
msgPrsId3Hint: 2.3 is read by every player and is what Mp3tag writes by default. 2.4 is the newer version and stores text as UTF-8. Both keep a repeated field as separate values.
lblStgNotify: Show notification when conversion is finished
msgClnRemoveTagsHint: One name per line (or separated by ;), as your tag editor shows it (COMMENT, ENCODERSETTINGS, LYRICS). Known names are suggested as you type; click one to use it. A * matches any text: REPLAYGAIN_*. Names are not case sensitive.
msgMngReorderHint: Drag an entry to change the order. The same order is used in the lists of the window.
tipMainParallel: Files converted at the same time
tipMainDestination: Where the converted files are written
tipMainOverwrite: What to do when the output file already exists
msgFxSilenceEndHint: The song is cut where it stops and exactly this much silence follows, so the tracks of an album are well separated in any player.
lblFxSilenceSeconds: Seconds of silence after the song
lblFxSilenceThreshold: Counts as silence below (dB under full scale)
lblFxSilenceMargin: Keep this much of the old ending (ms)
lblFxTarget: Target loudness (LUFS under full scale: 16 means -16 LUFS)
msgFxReplayGainHint: Writes the track gain and peak as tags; the sound itself is not changed. Players such as MusicBee level the volume from them.
msgFxTrimSilenceHint: Cuts the silence before the sound starts and after it stops. Silence inside the song is never touched.
lblFxTrimMargin: Keep this much silence at each cut (ms)
msgFxCutRangeHint: Keeps only the part between the two times, counted from what is left after the effects above it.
msgFxLimitHint: Keeps at most this many seconds, from the start.
msgFxVolumeHint: Sets how loud the track is, in one of four ways. A limiter follows any gain that could clip.
lblFxUseAlbum: Use the album's gain (same folder, same album tag)
msgFxFadeInHint: Raises the sound from silence over this long, at the start of what is kept.
msgFxFadeOutHint: Lowers the sound to silence over this long, at the end of what is kept.
msgFxChannelsHint: Changes how the two channels are used: swap them, play one on both sides (a mono source on both sides too), or mix them into one.
msgFxRepairHint: Removes short clicks and rebuilds peaks that were cut flat. Real restoration: it takes longer than the other effects.
msgFxLowCutHint: Removes the sound below a frequency: rumble, hum and a constant offset of old transfers.
msgFxDenoiseHint: Lowers steady noise such as hiss or a fan. It can leave artefacts on music; try a small reduction first.
msgFxDeEsserHint: Softens harsh "s" sounds in a voice.
msgFxEqualizerHint: Ten bands, an octave each: a gain in dB for every band, from -12 to +12.
msgFxToneHint: Raises or lowers the low and the high end, in dB.
msgFxDynamicsHint: A compressor lowers what is above a threshold; a dynamic normaliser evens the level out over the track. Either can ruin a track if pushed.
msgFxTempoHint: Plays faster or slower with the pitch kept. The track becomes shorter or longer.
